info.description: Crush is a terminal-based AI coding assistant. This API is served over a Unix socket (or Windows named pipe) and provides programmatic access to workspaces, sessions, agents, LSP, MCP, and more.

dimensions.description:
Dimensions is the size of the output vector for embedding models.
For embedding models that support multiple output sizes this is the
default/recommended dimensionality. It is zero for chat models.

image.description:
Image holds per-model image-input constraints. When zero, callers
should resolve the provider-family defaults via
[Model.ResolveImageLimits]; non-zero fields override those
defaults (e.g. newer Claude models that allow a larger long edge).

long_context_cost_per_1m_in.description:
Long context pricing (when >200K input tokens with 1M context enabled).
These are the premium rates; standard rates are in the CostPer1M* fields above.

supports_1m_context.description: Supports1MContext indicates the model supports the 1M context window beta feature.

seq.description:
Seq increases with every advertisement from the member; an older or
equal Seq never replaces a stored record.

addrs.description:
Addrs are host:port pairs built from the bound listener address: a
specific bind is its own host only, a wildcard bind every direct
endpoint host of the member.

endpoints.description:
Endpoints are Addrs classified by the advertising member, which
knows its own interfaces (additive: older members omit it).

device.description:
Device is the member's own advertisement of its device listeners
(nil: the member predates advertising).

rtt_ms.description: RTTMillis is the last mesh round-trip time; -1 when unknown.

autobalance.description:
Autobalance moves each new `crush run` job to the least loaded
online node before its first turn starts.

autobalance_margin.description:
AutobalanceMargin is how much better (on a 0-1 load score) another
node must be before a job moves; nil uses the default.

dimensions.description:
Dimensions optionally requests a specific output dimensionality for
models that support it. Zero means the model default.

hybrid_search.description:
HybridSearch controls whether search surfaces fuse the semantic
(vector) signal with substring matching. Nil means the default
(true when an embedder is configured). When false, search is pure
substring and no query embeddings are computed. Toggling this does
NOT invalidate stored vectors (it is not part of the signature).

model.description: Model is the embedding model id as used by the provider API.

normalize.description:
Normalize requests unit-normalized vectors (so cosine reduces to a
dot product) for models that support it.

provider.description:
Provider is the provider id, matching a key in the providers
config (same semantics as SelectedModel.Provider).

matcher.description: Regex pattern tested against the tool name. Empty means match all.

headers.description:
Headers are HTTP headers for HTTP/SSE MCP servers. Values run
through shell expansion at MCP startup, so $VAR and $(cmd)
work. A header whose value resolves to the empty string (unset
bare $VAR under lenient nounset, $(echo), or literal "") is
omitted from the outgoing request rather than sent as
"Header:".

oauth.description:
OAuth enables the MCP OAuth 2.1 authorization flow for HTTP
transport servers. When true, the client uses dynamic client
registration and opens a browser for the user to authorize.
Tokens are persisted automatically. Only supported for type=http.

oauth_callback_port.description:
OAuthCallbackPort pins the localhost port used for the OAuth
redirect listener. Set this when the OAuth provider requires an
exact-match callback URL (e.g. GitHub OAuth Apps). When omitted,
Crush picks the first free port from its default range.

oauth_client_id.description:
OAuthClientID is an optional pre-registered OAuth client ID. Set
it for servers that do not support dynamic client registration
(e.g. GitHub, Slack) and instead issue client credentials when you
register an OAuth app. Values run through shell expansion, so
$VAR and $(cmd) work.

oauth_client_secret.description:
OAuthClientSecret is the optional secret paired with
OAuthClientID for confidential clients. Values run through shell
expansion, so $VAR and $(cmd) work.

oauth_token.description:
OAuthToken is the persisted OAuth token for this server. It is
managed internally and stored in the global data config.

if_exists.description: IfExists is a file to check for before running the command.

run.description: Run is the command to execute.

model.description:
The model id as used by the provider API.
Required.

provider.description:
The model provider, same as the key/id used in the providers config.
Required.

reasoning_effort.description: Only used by models that use the openai provider and need this set.

think.description: Used by anthropic models that can reason to indicate if the model should think.

enabled.description: Enabled enables automatic snapshots on user messages.

exclude.description: Exclude is a list of glob patterns to exclude from snapshots.

low_bandwidth.description:
LowBandwidth, when true, swaps the animated spinner for a simple
"Generating .", "..", "..." cycle, halves the renderer FPS, and
disables the session-title reveal animation. Useful over slow
links or when the user wants reduced motion. Toggleable from the
command palette and forced on by the CRUSH_LOW_BANDWIDTH env var.

sessions_sidebar_width.description:
SessionsSidebarWidth is the width in columns of the left session
navigator, persisted so a resize survives restarts. Zero means use
the built-in default.

theme.description:
Theme selects the UI color theme by name. Builtin themes ("charmtone",
"hypercrush") and user themes from $config/crush/themes/*.lua are
supported. Local config overrides global, so a theme can be set
per-workspace. Empty falls back to the provider-derived default.

api_key.description:
APIKey is the xAI API key used to mint ephemeral voice secrets. It
is shell-expanded at request time ($XAI_API_KEY, $(cmd)). When
empty, XAI_API_KEY, then the Grok OAuth login, then the xai or
grok provider api_key are used.

base_url.description: BaseURL overrides the xAI API base URL.

enabled.description: Enabled controls whether worktrees are used (default true).

post_create.description: PostCreate defines commands to run after creating/restoring a worktree.

createWorktree.description: CreateWorktree if true, creates a new worktree with the snapshot state.

messageID.description:
MessageID is the message to fork from. The new session will include
all messages up to and including this one.

sessionID.description: SessionID is the source session to fork from.

title.description: Title is the title for the new session. Auto-generated if empty.

worktreeName.description: WorktreeName is the name for the new worktree. Auto-generated if empty.

models.description:
Keys are "large", "small", the optional "worker", and any
user-defined role names (see ModelRoles). Role names are the
vocabulary the `model` parameter on the agent/review tools
accepts, so an operator can map e.g. "scout" to a cheap model on
one machine and a different one on another without prompts
changing.

recent_models.description: Recently used models stored in the data directory config.

data_directory.description:
DataDirectory is where Crush keeps per-project state such as
the SQLite database and workspace overrides. Relative paths are
resolved against the working directory; absolute paths are used
verbatim. After defaulting the stored value is always absolute.

hosts.description: Hosts pins the hosts (or host:port) the locator advertises.

Hosts pins the hosts (or host:port) the offer advertises, in
preference order, instead of the detected ones.

kind.description: Kind is lan, wireguard, tailscale, vpn, bridge, public, or override.

priority.description:
Priority orders endpoints: lower is preferred (0 is an operator
override). Absent (0) from older nodes, which list best first.

device_ports.description:
DevicePorts says where Endpoints and NATSURLs come from:
"advertised" (the member's own record), "legacy" (the member
predates advertising; the pairing node's ports on its hosts), or
"unknown" (a record version this node does not know; both empty).
Absent from older pairing nodes.

nats_endpoints.description: NATSEndpoints are NATSURLs classified, in the same order.

nats_urls.description: NATSURLs are the member's device websocket URLs (wss://host:port).

ca_certs.description:
CACerts are the cluster CA certificates (DER), current first. A
device trusts one only if its SPKI hash is a pinned fingerprint.

client_id.description:
ClientID identifies the client that initiated the turn. The
server uses it to route per-client resources (notably the editor
bridge) to the right client. Empty means "no specific client".

permission_policy.description:
PermissionPolicy, when set, is the permission policy for this turn
and the sub-agents it spawns: "allow" approves every request,
"deny" denies anything not pre-approved, and "prompt" always asks
a client, even when the workspace skips prompts. It applies only
to this turn (also when the turn is queued behind another), never
to other turns on the session.

swarm_parts.description:
SwarmParts, when set, replaces the default TextContent user
message with one or more [SwarmMessage] parts. Used by
[Backend.SwarmSend] so the receiving session records
structured sender metadata (color, animal, workspace) instead
of a plain text prefix. The Prompt field must still be set to
the concatenated user-visible text so downstream code that
treats prompts as strings (queue drop notifications, run
logs) keeps working.

color.description:
Color and Animal are the session's swarm identity (see
[session.Session.Color] / .Animal). Empty when the session
has not yet been backfilled; UI code should fall back to no
address label / no color square in that case.

model_ref.description:
ModelRef is the model reference the session was spawned with (see
[session.Session.ModelRef]); empty when it runs the workspace's
large model.

owner_node.description:
OwnerNode is the cluster node that owns the session (empty = the
server answering).

client_id.description:
ClientID is stamped by the device bridge; any device-supplied value
is replaced.

next_before.description:
NextBefore is the `before` value for the next (older) page; null
when this page reaches the first message.

data_dir.description: DataDir is omitted from slim rows (fields=row).

workspace_id.description:
WorkspaceID is set only while the workspace is attached; it is a
runtime handle, not a stable identifier.

has_more.description: HasMore is set when NextCursor is.

next_cursor.description: NextCursor fetches the next page; null on the last page.

reset.description:
Reset says the since cursor is unusable as a whole (malformed, from
a restarted node, or older than the retained change window): do a
full fetch. Sessions and Deleted are empty.

reset_nodes.description:
ResetNodes are nodes whose full list is included in Sessions: the
client replaces every row of those nodes (after the last page).

stale_nodes.description:
StaleNodes are nodes that could not be asked; their rows and cursor
positions are unchanged.

sync_cursor.description:
SyncCursor is an opaque position for a later since request. Absent
from servers that predate delta sync, and on a reset.

code.description:
Code is a machine-readable error code, when the route defines one
(for example [ErrCodeSessionNotOnNode]).

gc.description:
GC garbage-collects the Crush snapshot repository before sending,
so unreachable snapshot objects are not shipped.

resume.description: Resume continues a paused in-flight turn on the destination.

target_node.description: TargetNode is the destination cluster node ID.

configured.description: Configured reports that the workspace config has this provider.

has_credential.description:
HasCredential reports that an API key or OAuth token is set; the
credential itself is never returned.

oauth.description: OAuth reports that the credential is an OAuth token.

all_workspaces.description:
AllWorkspaces opts into cross-workspace fan-out: when true the
backend also searches every other known workspace (attached and
registry-detached) and merges the results. When false (the
default) only the requested workspace is searched — the fast path.

offset.description:
Offset is reserved: session-level pagination is not yet supported
(results collapse per session after a message-level candidate
fetch, so a message offset would not align to session boundaries).
It is currently ignored by the backend.

fallback_reason.description:
FallbackReason says why Mode is "text": no_embedder,
disabled_by_request, disabled_by_config, no_embeddings, or
embed_error.

mode.description:
Mode is the search mode actually used: "hybrid" (substring and
vector signals fused) or "text" (substring only).

semantic_used.description:
SemanticUsed reports whether the vector signal ran without error.
Kept for older clients; prefer Mode.

configured.description: Configured reports whether at least one AI provider is enabled.

color.description:
Color and Animal are the session's swarm identity (see
[session.Session.Color] / .Animal). Empty when the session
has not yet been backfilled; UI code should fall back to no
address label / no color square in that case.

model_ref.description:
ModelRef is the model reference the session was spawned with (see
[session.Session.ModelRef]); empty when it runs the workspace's
large model.

owner_node.description:
OwnerNode is the cluster node that owns the session (empty = the
server answering).

default.description:
Default reports that the session follows the workspace's large
model (no ModelRef, or one that no longer resolves).

large.description:
Large is the model the session's top-level turns run on: the
resolved ModelRef, else the workspace's large model.

model_ref.description:
ModelRef is the session's own model reference; empty when the
session follows the workspace's large model.

small.description:
Small is the model used for the session's titles and summaries. It
is always the workspace's small model.

model.description: Model selects a provider and model explicitly.

model_ref.description: ModelRef is a role name, "provider/model", or a bare model id.

model_type.description:
ModelType is the slot to set; only "large" (the default) is
per-session.

color.description:
Color and Animal are the session's swarm identity (see
[session.Session.Color] / .Animal). Empty when the session
has not yet been backfilled; the picker/sidebar should fall
back to no color square in that case.

favorite.description:
Favorite pins the session to the top of the sidebar inbox (below
sessions blocked on a permission prompt). It is read from the
session's database (attached or detached) so it persists.

owner_node.description:
OwnerNode is the cluster node that owns (may write) the session; ""
means the node that produced this overview. OwnerName is its
display name. ReadOnly marks a replica shown because its owner is
unreachable.

replica_reason.description:
ReplicaReason explains a ReadOnly replica, e.g. "owner unreachable:
context deadline exceeded". OwnerUnreachableSince is when this node
started failing to reach the owner (unix ms; 0 if unknown).

client_id.description:
ClientID identifies the client that initiated the command so the
server can run it in that client's launch directory. Multiple
clients can share one workspace (subdirectories or sibling git
worktrees collapsing to the same project root); without it the
command would run in whichever client created the workspace first.

path.description:
Path is the workspace's project root; clients connect to it to
operate on the session.

persistent.description:
Persistent is true when the server runs as a daemon that does not
exit after its last workspace closes.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is the secret's expiry in unix seconds.

node_id.description:
NodeID and NodeName identify the cluster node that owns the
workspace. Empty means the server answering the request.

stale.description:
Stale marks a remote node's last good overview served because the
latest refresh failed; StaleSince is when it was fetched (unix ms)
and LastError why the refresh failed. On a node-level Unavailable
marker StaleSince is the last successful fetch, if any.

unavailable.description:
Unavailable marks a workspace (or, with an empty Root, a whole
cluster node) whose sessions could not be read in time; Error says
why. Sessions is then empty or a stale subset.
